requirement:
Each first-party Rust file under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing` MUST have at least 80%
execution coverage of its instrumented lines, or current accepted exception
evidence explaining why the file falls below that target under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Counts MUST use the
file-and-line union rule of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`;
a line counts as executed when any eligible test process or its associated
child processes has a positive execution count for it.

The check MUST use the combined selection and freshness rules of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, restricted to the active
build configuration. It MUST compare exact counts rather than rounded displayed
percentages, average file percentages, or impose an 80% target within each
function. A file whose executable code is not measured MUST require exception
evidence rather than pass with a fabricated percentage. A file established to
contain no executable coverage obligations MUST be reported as such and MUST
NOT require a threshold exception.
Absence of recorded instrumented lines alone MUST NOT establish that a file
contains no executable coverage obligations.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold` has no structural obligations, so no implementation root is needed. I checked each clause for a library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or named-interface delegation that a behavior-preserving alternative could violate. I found none.

- "Each first-party Rust file … MUST have at least 80% execution coverage of its instrumented lines, or current accepted exception evidence": this is an observable pass/fail outcome. Any implementation that gives the same verdicts satisfies it.
- "Counts MUST use the file-and-line union rule of `requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`; a line counts as executed when any eligible test process or its associated child processes has a positive execution count": this is a counting semantic. An implementation could compute the union in SQL, in memory, or incrementally and give the same counts. The union rule itself is defined and cited in `requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`, so it is context here. It does not prescribe a structure for this requirement.
- "MUST use the combined selection and freshness rules of `requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and `requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, restricted to the active build configuration": this specifies which results are eligible. Any code that filters the same way behaves identically. Those declarations carry their own obligations, such as the SQLite snapshot.
- "MUST compare exact counts rather than rounded displayed percentages, average file percentages, or impose an 80% target within each function": this constrains the observable verdict. A cross-multiplied integer comparison and an exact rational comparison give identical results. Neither names a type or API.
- "A file whose executable code is not measured MUST require exception evidence rather than pass with a fabricated percentage", "A file established to contain no executable coverage obligations MUST be reported as such and MUST NOT require a threshold exception", and "Absence of recorded instrumented lines alone MUST NOT establish that a file contains no executable coverage obligations": these are classification and reporting outcomes. They do not dictate how the classification is built.

The remaining declarations (`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing`, `requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`) are cited for context. They define the file scope and the exception policy, and they are assessed against their own text. Behavioral coverage of the clauses above is left to the test-adequacy criterion.

behavioral: The reviewed tests cover each behavioral obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`. I did not find a gap.

- **At least 80% per file, exact counts.** `exact_per_file_threshold_and_partial_functions` asserts `threshold(79_999,100_000)` is false even though it would display 80.0%. It asserts 80,000/100,000 is true and 0/0 is false. It checks a 4/5 file passes. It shows another file's higher percentage cannot rescue `driver.rs`: 0/1 gives FAIL, and 7/10 gives FAIL even though the 85% average of the two files would pass. The same test confirms the executed function has no `#fn[driver]` item.
- **No 80% target within each function.** `a_function_below_eighty_percent_needs_no_exception_when_its_file_passes` has a function at 1/3 in a file at 10/12. It asserts the report passes and lists no accepted exceptions.
- **Union rule, child processes and filtered runs.** `children_and_filtered_runs_contribute_to_the_same_union` combines a parent and a child process, which gives 5/5. A later all-zero filtered run leaves 5/5 and a pass.
- **Selection, freshness and active build configuration.** `inactive_and_stale_measurements_cannot_raise_the_file_total` checks four cases:
  - An inactive old build cannot raise the total (0/1 FAIL).
  - A stale success beside a fresh failure still reports `stale coverage` and does not pass.
  - A recorded build that disagrees with the active build makes the store unavailable.
  - Failure text appears in each case.
  `stale_missing_legacy_and_invalid_store_cannot_use_older_success` also covers missing, legacy, stale and invalid stores.
- **Exception evidence.** `accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution`, `missing_and_stale_explanations_fail_the_report` and `function_explanations_never_transfer_to_other_functions_or_the_file` cover these cases:
  - An accepted file exception passes a below-threshold file but does not excuse its functions.
  - Missing, rejected, `{fixme}` or stale reviews still FAIL.
  - An accepted exception for a not-measured file is reported as `not measured — accepted exception`.
- **Unmeasured executable file.** `unmeasured_executable_files_and_parse_failures_do_not_disappear` asserts `code.rs: not measured — FAIL` for `fn missing(){}` with no recorded lines, with no fabricated percentage. `measured_file_threshold_remains_checked_when_source_parsing_fails` and the malformed-source case in the same test show parse failures are not silently skipped.
- **No executable obligations.** A file with only `struct S; trait T { fn declaration(); }` is reported as `no executable obligations — pass`. `default_trait_bodies_and_cfg_exclusions_are_obligations_but_declarations_are_not` shows trait default bodies and cfg-excluded functions are obligations, and declarations are not.
- **Absent lines alone do not establish no obligations.** The `missing` function case above and the `inventory` assertions cover this. `inventory` returns false for a macro invocation and for a derive attribute, and true for a plain struct plus declaration.

The macro and derive cases are asserted at the `inventory` level, not through the report. `inventory` is where the no-obligations decision is made, so I count that as adequate.

Each first-party Rust file under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing` MUST have at least 80%
execution coverage of its instrumented lines, or current accepted exception
evidence explaining why the file falls below that target under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Counts MUST use the
file-and-line union rule of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`;
a line counts as executed when any eligible test process or its associated
child processes has a positive execution count for it.
The check MUST use the combined selection and freshness rules of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, restricted to the active
build configuration. It MUST compare exact counts rather than rounded displayed
percentages, average file percentages, or impose an 80% target within each
function. A file whose executable code is not measured MUST require exception
evidence rather than pass with a fabricated percentage. A file established to
contain no executable coverage obligations MUST be reported as such and MUST
NOT require a threshold exception.
Absence of recorded instrumented lines alone MUST NOT establish that a file
contains no executable coverage obligations.
:::{req} rust_item_coverage.parsing
Repository validation parses every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs`
file among the sources reference discovery considers under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root
`vendor` directory. It reports a Rust parse failure rather than silently
skipping the file.
:::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
:::{req} index.summary
Saved execution-coverage checks compute line coverage from the union of
instrumented file-and-line locations in the eligible current results under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, including child processes.
Each location counts once in the denominator and is covered when any selected
process has a positive execution count. Percentages use these union counts,
rather than averaging process reports.
When the current set has no usable instrumented lines, or any current result
has unavailable measurements under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.measurement`, combined coverage is
reported as unavailable. The check does not publish measured coverage
percentages or threshold results computed from only the remaining readable
results. Otherwise, absent file or function measurements remain subject to
their coverage obligations.
:::{req} index.selection
Saved execution-coverage checks read the current coverage set under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.current` from SQLite. Each check
uses one coherent database snapshot of test identities, states, provenance,
and processed measurements, so a replacement or update cannot mix results
from different snapshots within the same check.
Checks do not search historical runs or use a separate report-selection
metadata cache. Current test identities, states, and provenance can be read
without loading their detailed measurements.
Only current results with complete, available measurements contribute to
coverage under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`.
Pending, running, and unavailable entries are reported under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.measurement`. Checking does not build
or execute tests and never restores a superseded attempt.
:::{req} index.freshness
Only current results whose captured source inputs match the current source
and whose build configurations are compatible contribute counts to saved
execution-coverage checks under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`. Results with changed
inputs are identified as stale; results of unknown compatibility are
identified as unavailable. Both are excluded from combined totals.
A filtered run preserves the provenance of unselected results under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace`. It does not make those
results fresh when their recorded inputs no longer match. Their process
reports and matching captured source remain available until replacement or
removal of the build artifacts.
